regression_risks: Persistence: dismissed_at is written as an aware datetime.now(UTC). SQLAlchemy's SQLite DateTime drops tzinfo and stores the same string format as last_played_at, so the string comparison dismissed_at < last_played_at stays consistent. A different backend (not SQLite) would need re-checking.
Concurrency: dismiss is a single-row read-then-write. A POST /progress that lands in the same instant could order either way. This is outside the single-user threat model.

test_coverage: Migration: three tests cover an old DB gaining a NULL column with no rows lost, a second startup as a no-op, and a fresh DB (test_database_migration_dismissed_at.py).
